decisions.summary: Wave 43 takes rows 482-485 in ranking order, rows 486-492 next
decisions.why: A contiguous run of E2 rows in ranking order (FR-006, SC-003).

decisions.summary: fold_the_connector_hairpin re-lays the lane onto the connector's first leg as a T (tee), and the connector stays
decisions.why: 0081.drawing: 'the arriving lane meets the other's side as a T instead'. The old fold still met end to end at b. The test asserts the end lies on the connector's side, more than 1.5 ft from its start. This is the ranked fix.

decisions.summary: No fold where the T's link is not walkable or the overlap matrix refuses it; the hairpin stands
decisions.why: Physical impossibility. A T laid through a steading breaks 0246's 'nothing built on a lane' (the matrix and tee's footprint clearance). A hairpin left standing is not accepted silently: law.connector_hairpin_ends (0081) still flags it and last_resort.py:79 treats the lane as bad. The refusal was already there before this wave.

decisions.summary: next_gather's third form (teed_onto) reapplied from wave 28's 183792b7c
decisions.why: This is ranking row 483's fix word for word. Wave 28 reverted it only because the polder change it was bundled with was held, and that hold was later withdrawn (a465b644c). The reason was never the knot form itself.

decisions.summary: reach_to_steading: within 60 ft of the house's footprint, or 12 ft of the built ground recorded 'of' it; fronting_ends (and fronted_ends through it) reads it
decisions.why: 0246.drawing: 'within 60 ft of the house, or within 12 ft of the steading's built ground - its house, byre, shed, threshing yard or garden'. The ranked fix is implemented. Reading 'of the house' as the house's footprint is a plain reading of the page's words.

decisions.summary: DOORSTEP_FT (80 ft from center) kept for its other readers (settle.py:132/406/852, corridors.py:392)
decisions.why: None of these readers claims 0246's reach. Two carry UNRESEARCHED claims (the fence exemption at settle.py:136 and the fan cut in settle_ends). One is an index search radius, and one finds a route's own dooryard. All are outside row 484.

decisions.summary: DOORSTEP_FT's own docstring and claim left untouched: 'A free lane end this near a farmhouse's center is discharged by that house ... an end discharged by a house - GUESS 0246: within 80 ft of its center'
decisions.why: dev/claims-index.json already holds law.py::DOORSTEP_FT#an end discharged by a house as DRIFTED (2026-10-07). Its note is the same 0246 60/12 mismatch that row 484 fixes. That finding appears in neither ranking.json nor any found-*.jsonl. After this wave no code discharges an end by DOORSTEP_FT, so its docstring and claim describe behavior the code no longer has, and still cite 0246 for an 80 ft figure the page does not contain. The wave fixed the rule and left its twin claim false and unfiled. Nothing makes the literal fix impossible: restating the claim takes one line. Fix in this wave: restate DOORSTEP_FT's docstring and claim to what its remaining readers use it for, each with its own label (the fence exemption and the fan cut are UNRESEARCHED), re-checked by impl-drift at T112; or file it as a found row tiered by a fresh reader, as T111a does. The fan cut (settle.py:406) still cuts an end back past 80 ft from the center, while fronting is now measured to footprints and built ground. The restated claim must say that honestly.

decisions.summary: _lay_web_lane: a run within 25 ft of the network whose straight snap is not walkable is refused, not drawn stopping short
decisions.why: 0081.drawing: 'Ends within 25 ft of one another are joined at a single point'. Before this wave, the run was drawn with a gap and counted as arriving; that gap is gone. The refusal of the run is the tail of row 486's ranked fix ('lays a routed link as the far-gap branch does (clear_runs) or refuses the run'). Row 486 is the next row. Condition: row 486 stays owed. Its routed link must be tried before this refusal, and the claim's 'or not drawn where that link is not walkable' must become 'where no link is walkable'. Row 486 must not be marked already fixed by wave 43.

decisions.summary: Wave 42's found row (brook_rules.py::ditch_strokes) tiered E3 by a fresh reader and left for its place
decisions.why: Process under FR-002/FR-003 and SC-003, the same as earlier found-row tiering. The reasons given for E3 (per-channel width carried across brook_rules.py and brook.py) match FR-003's 'a change across modules'.

decisions.summary: No review occasions: the five hamlets were regenerated with byte-identical manifests after each change
decisions.why: The occasions follow from what the maps drew (feature 294). The plan states a measurement, not an exemption. This narrows nothing the GM asked for.
